**Visual observations from test image:**
- Multiple soybean plants showing collapse/wilting in the center of the frame
- Bleached/white dead stems visible
- Dead brown leaves remaining attached to stems (not fallen)
- Surrounding plants appear healthy and green — typical "patch" pattern
- Some white cottony material visible on the dying stems

**Reasoning:**
The combination of bleached white stems, dead leaves remaining attached, patch-collapse pattern, and visible white mycelial growth on stems strongly aligns with **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot). The description matches: "dry dead stems develop a bleached white appearance... dead leaves remain attached to stems while turning completely brown." The reference image confirms white stem coating with black sclerotia — consistent with what's seen in the test image's center plants.
